source.title_on_document: Competition and Diversity in Generative AI

paper_design_summary: A game-theoretic model in which n producers each sample content from a generative AI tool and earn less when others produce the same content type; the paper proves that stronger competition yields more diverse equilibrium output (Sections 3 to 5). It then simulates the game with six small open-source language models playing Scattergories, where each simulated player chooses a sampling temperature (and, in Section 6.2, a model), with a seventh model judging answer validity. No human participants take part, and no person receives AI help.

studies.label: Theory plus language-model simulation of Scattergories (Sections 3 to 6)

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people assigned. Simulated players are language models whose sampling temperature (and model choice in Section 6.2) is varied by the author.
assignment.quote: Our empirical setup is simple: n players each use an LLM to generate a single response to a Scattergories instance given by a (letter, category) pair.

participants.exclusions: No human participants. Inputs are 25 randomly sampled (letter, category) Scattergories instances (Table 2, p. 85) and 2,000 samples per (language model, temperature, instance) combination (p. 19).
participants.who: No human participants; six language models (gemma2, llama3.1, llama3.2, mistral, nemotron, phi3.5) act as players and qwen2.5 validates answers.
participants.quote: Our experiments compare six LLMs, each of which is a relatively small open-source language model

ai_tool.name_model: gemma-2-2b-it, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, Nemotron-Mini-4B-Instruct, Phi-3.5-mini-instruct; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as validator
ai_tool.how_used: Models generate Scattergories answers at temperatures in steps of 0.05; utilities and equilibria are computed from the sampled answers. No human uses the models.

task.description: Scattergories: give a word or phrase that starts with a given letter and fits a given category; a player scores only with a valid answer that others did not give (score function s_gamma(x) = x^gamma).

eligibility.reason: Theory paper with a model-only simulation: language models play Scattergories against each other (p. 17-18, Section 6). No human participants, no assignment of people to AI, and no human-produced output is scored. Model-only and theory papers are listed in the screening report and omitted from the dataset (codebook Section 3).

one_line_finding: In a game-theoretic model, stronger competition yields more diverse equilibrium output, though less diverse than socially optimal (Theorems 4.3 to 4.5, pp. 12-13); in Scattergories simulations with six language models, equilibrium temperatures rise with the number of players, and llama3.1, best alone (valid answer 92 percent of the time vs. 68 percent for phi3.5), loses market share to phi3.5 as players increase (pp. 20-21, Figures 4 to 6).
notes: No human participants anywhere in the paper, appendices included (Sections 6, C.1 to C.3, pp. 17-25 and 83-97). The prompt-robustness check in Section 6.3 uses 10 extra prompts written by five chatbots (p. 88). No data or code link is given in the document.
